extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, administrative law practitioners, and litigants (Montana administrative law/MAPA context)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards under the Montana Administrative Procedure Act (MAPA) for filing and litigating petitions for judicial review, appeals, declaratory rulings, subpoenas/discovery, representation, and related agency practice. Focused on requirements, timing, grounds, and evidentiary rules used by courts and agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing petition for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings for review shall be instituted by filing a petition in district court within 30 days after service of the final decision of the agency or, if a rehearing is requested, within 30 days after the decision thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory filing deadline; courts have treated agency conduct (e.g., failure to give notice or form of final decision) as estopping an agency from asserting untimely filing. Filing both a petition and a motion for reconsideration/rehearing is sometimes done to preserve rights where rehearing rules are unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue for petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided by statute, the petition shall be filed in the district court for the county where the petitioner resides or has his principal place of business or where the agency maintains its principal office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory exceptions may exist; case law has interpreted whether particular appeals are 'actions against the county' affecting venue rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of petition copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the petition shall be promptly served upon the agency and all parties of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt service on the agency and all parties of record is required after filing; service procedures generally follow civil rules (see service of pleadings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of petition for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition shall include a concise statement of the facts upon which jurisdiction and venue are based, a statement of the manner in which the petitioner is aggrieved, and the ground or grounds specified in subsection (7) upon which the petitioner contends he is entitled to relief. The petition shall demand the relief to which the petitioner believes he is entitled, and the demand for relief may be in the alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute sets minimum allegations; Form 13 in the appendix is a sample petition. If seeking stay or other intermediate relief, attach final agency order and possibly affidavits of injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing on enforcement and stays
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by statute, the filing of the petition shall not stay enforcement of the agency's decision. The agency may grant or the reviewing court may order a stay upon terms which it considers proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some statutes provide automatic stays during judicial review; McCrory inserted a savings phrase to reflect that. Appellants sometimes attach stay motions or seek rehearing simultaneously to preserve options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency transmission and scope of the record
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after service of the petition (or further time allowed by the court), the agency shall transmit to the reviewing court the original or a certified copy of the entire record of the proceeding under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By stipulation of all parties the record may be shortened; a party unreasonably refusing to stipulate may be taxed for additional costs. The court may require or permit corrections or additions to the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave to present additional evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If, before the hearing, application is made to the court for leave to present additional evidence and it is shown to the satisfaction of the court that the additional evidence is material and that there were good reasons for failure to present it before the agency, the court may order the additional evidence be taken before the agency upon conditions determined by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional evidence leads the agency to modify findings/decision, it shall file the evidence and any modifications with the reviewing court. The standard requires materiality and good cause for prior non-presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review confined to the record; oral argument and briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The review shall be conducted by the court without a jury and shall be confined to the record. In cases of alleged irregularities in procedure before the agency not shown in the record, proof may be taken in court. The court, upon request, shall hear oral argument and receive written briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-trial conferences can shorten transcripts/identify parties. Typically parties move for judgment on the pleadings or summary judgment after the record is certified; argument proceeds on the court's calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground (a): violation of constitutional or statutory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may reverse or modify the decision if substantial rights of the appellant have been prejudiced because the administrative findings, inferences, conclusions, or decisions are in violation of constitutional or statutory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core legal ground for reversal tying agency action to constitutional/statutory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground (b): excess of statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may reverse or modify if the administrative findings, inferences, conclusions, or decisions are in excess of the statutory authority of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where agencies act beyond delegated powers or statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground (c): made upon unlawful procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may reverse or modify if the administrative findings, inferences, conclusions, or decisions were made upon unlawful procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural due process defects; irregularities not shown in the record may still be proven in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground (d): affected by other error of law
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may reverse or modify if the administrative findings, inferences, conclusions, or decisions were affected by other error of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catches various legal errors not otherwise categorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground (e): clearly erroneous on the whole record
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may reverse or modify if findings are clearly erroneous in view of the reliable, probative, and substantial evidence on the whole record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'clearly erroneous' standard is defined: a finding is clearly erroneous when, although there is evidence to support it, the reviewing court on the entire evidence is left with a definite and firm conviction that a mistake has been committed. This standard permits setting aside 'clearly' erroneous decisions but does not permit reweighing the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground (f): arbitrary, capricious, or abuse of discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may reverse or modify if the decision was arbitrary or capricious or characterized by abuse of discretion or clearly unwarranted exercise of discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard addresses agency decisions lacking rational basis or abusing discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground (g): failure to make requested findings of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may reverse or modify if findings of fact, upon issues essential to the decision, were not made although requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires showing that findings were essential and were properly requested of the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Supreme Court: timing and stay rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An aggrieved party may obtain review of a final judgment of a district court by appeal to the supreme court within 60 days after entry of judgment. Stay rules: (1) if appeal is from a judgment affirming an agency decision, the agency decision shall not be stayed except upon order of the supreme court (with a 20-day automatic continuation if a stay existed at filing); (2) if appeal is from a judgment reversing or modifying an agency decision, the agency decision shall be stayed pending final determination unless the supreme court orders otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the manner provided by law for civil appeals; special rules govern stays during appellate proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency declaratory rulings procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide by rule for the filing and prompt disposition of petitions for declaratory rulings as to the applicability of any statutory provision or of any rule or order of the agency. A declaratory ruling, or the refusal to issue such a ruling, shall be subject to judicial review in the same manner as decisions or orders in contested cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to help persons uncertain about potential violations; agencies' model rules vary on whether a hearing is required for a binding ruling; courts review agency declaratory rulings under the same standards as contested case decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory judgment on rule validity or applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may be declared invalid or inapplicable in a declaratory judgment action if it is found that the rule or its threatened application interferes with or impairs or threatens to interfere with or impair the legal rights or privileges of the plaintiff, or if the rule was adopted with an arbitrary or capricious disregard for the purpose of the authorizing statute as evidenced by documented legislative intent. If the administrative code committee has objected to the rule on such grounds, the agency bears the burden of proving its rule was not adopted with arbitrary or capricious disregard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action may be brought in county of plaintiff's residence, principal place of business, or agency principal office; the agency must be made a party; action may be brought whether or not the plaintiff requested the agency to pass on the rule first. The 1977 amendments added reverse-burden and documentation aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency subpoena power and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency conducting proceedings shall have power to require furnishing of information, attendance of witnesses, and production of books, records, papers, documents and other objects as may be necessary; an agency may issue subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum on its own motion or upon request of any party. Method of service, witness fees, and mileage shall be the same as in civil actions. Enforcement: agency or party may apply to district court for an order to compel compliance; court shall hear expeditiously; contempt available for disobedience of court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witness fees and mileage are paid by requesting party unless statute provides otherwise. If alternate statutory enforcement methods exist, they may be used as alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery in contested case hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide in its rules of practice for discovery prior to a contested case hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model rules often adopt civil discovery provisions, although some agencies encourage less formal data requests. Discovery may slow hearings but is required to permit adequate preparation; some tax appeal contexts limit discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person compelled to appear in person or who voluntarily appears before any agency shall be accorded the right to be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel. Every party shall be accorded the right to appear in person or by or with counsel, but the part shall not be construed as requiring an agency to furnish counsel to any such person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a uniform right to counsel in agency proceedings, though agencies are not required to provide counsel. Agencies may permit non-attorney representatives in some contexts (e.g., PSC practice or specific program rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of pleadings in agency proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where a statute expressly provides to the contrary, service in all agency proceedings subject to this part and in proceedings for judicial review thereof shall be as prescribed for civil actions in the district courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a matter becomes a contested case, service typically follows Rule 5 (certificate of mailing); petitions for judicial review are served under Rule 4. Some initial administrative filings may not fit Rule 4's summons format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and effect of the MAPA part
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this part shall be considered to limit or repeal requirements imposed by statute or otherwise recognized law. No subsequent legislation shall be considered to supersede or modify any provision of this part except to the extent such legislation does so expressly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves existing statutory requirements and requires express legislative language to override the part; conflicting laws are repealed to the extent of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and attachments for petitions (practical form guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 13 in the appendix is a sample petition for judicial review. If the pleader seeks a stay or other intermediate relief, he will probably attach a copy of the final agency order and perhaps an affidavit as to injury to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the sample forms in the appendix as models; attaching supporting documents helps when requesting interim relief such as stays.
